# BES Inward

> Behavioural Entropy Signatures turned inward. A system watches its own operator and asks "are you behaving like yourself?" instead of "who are you?". It learns the operator's behavioural signature (the mix of actions + the rhythm of them) as a one-class rolling baseline, then flags a run that is either too regular (scripted automation) or too far from the operator's mix (a hijack) — by behaviour, no credential. The baseline only folds in windows it already allowed, so an impostor cannot poison it (negative selection).

Live: https://sjgant80-hub.github.io/bes-inward/

## Proof (re-runnable)
- attack-kit/redteam.mjs --check: 6 cases, byte-identical — operator's own varied behaviour passes (low FP); scripted flagged (too regular); hijack flagged (uncorrelated); baseline unpoisonable; calibrates while learning; fails closed.
- witness-all.mjs: mutation + fuzz gate over bes.mjs — CLEAN, 46/49 killed, 3 reviewed-equivalent.
- test/*.test.mjs: unit + hostile-input (never-throw) suites.

## Lineage
BES = Gary W. Floyd (Lumiea Systems Research Division, ThunderStruck Services, LLC, "GEP-Based Security", 2025). The 4th security pillar after break-it (authentication) and perimeter-post (authorization). Konomi / Thomas Frumkin credited. MIT.
